rubrics.criterion: The per-destination name policy that previously lived only as private inline code inside individual output plugin implementations now has a single shared home: one shared module-level mechanism, located in the shared plugin contract package that all destination plugins already import or in a comparable shared location on the common import path of the destination plugins, and every affected destination plugin obtains its prepared destination names through it.
rubrics.rationale: This case's central obligation is moving a scattered responsibility into exactly one place; the plugin contract package that owns the shared {$} template resolution helper is the repository's existing shared anchor for destination plugins, so grading requires that the patch ends with a policy home that is genuinely shared rather than per-plugin.

rubrics.criterion: No destination plugin implements its own character-handling logic for names resolved from {$} configuration templates anymore: at each formerly affected site the plugin resolves (or passes on) the template value and delegates the name preparation to the shared mechanism, keeping at most name resolution and transport use in the plugin.
rubrics.rationale: The injected diff placed scrubbing logic directly inside plugin functions next to their template resolutions; unless the plugins stop owning that logic, the responsibility remains scattered no matter what shared code was added.

rubrics.criterion: Per-destination differences are expressed as declared data or parameters of the shared mechanism - allowed or replaced characters and their replacement, byte-length caps, case handling, and empty-name fallback - so two destinations with different rules differ only in what they declare to the shared mechanism, and a new destination's rules can be added as a new declaration alongside the existing ones.
rubrics.rationale: The maintenance scenario driving this case is repeated re-editing of differently shaped procedural copies; the outcome is only achieved if the differences between destinations are data in one place rather than twelve variants of logic, which is what makes 'add the next destination' a one-place change.

rubrics.criterion: Per-destination naming behavior is preserved exactly: for the same event row and configuration, each destination still produces the same name as before the refactor - the same characters are replaced with the same replacement character (or kept by the same whitelist), the same byte-length caps are applied, the same case normalization applies, the same fallback name is used when the resolved name is empty, and the same row is used for template resolution at each site.
rubrics.rationale: The task prompt promises behavior preservation because live pipelines depend on the exact names; a consolidation that quietly changes which characters a destination rejects, its cap, or its fallback silently breaks running pipelines and must not count as a resolution.

rubrics.criterion: Every destination-name write path that consumed the previously inline policy is migrated to the shared mechanism: the kafka message construction path's topic, the rabbitmq publish path's exchange, routing key and queue, the redis cache key path, the memcache key path, the mongodb write path's database and collection, the mongodb delete path's database and collection, the elasticsearch commit path's index, and the activemq STOMP publish path's destination.
rubrics.rationale: These are the concrete hidden responsibility locations the concern was injected into; leaving any one of them (most plausibly the mongodb delete path, whose current row is data.Rows[0] rather than the last row, or one of the three rabbitmq names) on private logic leaves the responsibility still split.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor removes the artifacts that existed only to support the inline policy: private helper methods, local closures, and package-level pattern variables whose sole purpose was the per-plugin scrubbing are deleted rather than left as dead code, and imports (or import blocks) that only those copies needed are dropped so each destination plugin still compiles cleanly.
rubrics.rationale: A consolidate-and-migrate that leaves the old copies in place keeps two parallel implementations of the policy, so the obsolete injected artifacts are an explicit part of completing this case's change.

rubrics.criterion: The shared mechanism is shaped so that adding naming rules for a further destination requires only a new declaration there plus the new destination's own code: the rule set reads as a fixed catalog, table, or parameterization the new destination plugs into, with no need to modify unrelated destination plugins or the mechanism's application code.
rubrics.rationale: The motivating maintenance scenario is onboarding more destinations; the quality bar for this case is that the next destination's name rules are a one-place addition, which is observable from how the shared mechanism's declarations and application path are factored.

rubrics.criterion: No destination plugin implementation package in the repository still contains its own copy of the {$}-resolved destination-name scrubbing policy: none of the twelve formerly affected name sites (nor any newly written equivalent block in a destination plugin) still replaces or filters the resolved name's characters with inline logic inside the plugin.
rubrics.rationale: The specific residue this smell leaves behind is per-plugin scrub code next to template resolutions; the checker-visible success condition of the case is that this class of copy no longer exists anywhere in the destination plugin packages after the solver patch.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not merely relocate the copies: the shared mechanism is not a thin wrapper that each plugin calls with its own still-private procedure, and the per-plugin blocks were not just renamed, reindented, or moved into per-plugin helper functions while keeping one procedural variant per destination.
rubrics.rationale: Plausible near-misses for this case are mechanical reshuffles labeled as consolidation - wrapping the same inline code in a call, or hoisting each block into its own per-plugin function - which leave the shotgun surgery intact; this item fails those while accepting any genuine centralization of the rule content.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor does not change the observable naming result of any destination: no destination gets a widened or narrowed character policy, a different cap, different case handling, or a different empty-name fallback than it had in the pre-refactor injected state, and no name-preparation step was disabled, short-circuited, or bypassed to make the consolidation easier.
rubrics.rationale: Behavior preservation is promised by the task prompt and is what separates a real consolidation from a rewrite; weakening a destination's policy (for example dropping the $-replacement on only one of the two mongodb paths, or forgetting the 255-byte clamp under one of the three rabbitmq names) is the characteristic regression this refactor invites.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not modify unrelated subsystems: the shared template-resolution primitive keeps its own semantics and signature-compatible behavior, the {$} row-value resolution feeding column mapping in the mysql and clickhouse plugins is untouched, input plugins and server-side routing/dispatch are untouched, the destination plugins' configuration parameter names and JSON tags stay compatible with existing saved configurations, and the transport messages/commands sent stay byte-for-byte identical for the same inputs.
rubrics.rationale: A consolidation in this repository is one rewire of destination plugin call sites plus new shared code; anything that reaches into template resolution itself, the row-value column mapping that also uses {$} references, or configuration formats is out-of-scope collateral that would break user setups and must fail the item.
